knowledge:
- key_parameters: tol=Radius of hyperspheres in countCells, typically set to 0.5 times the square root of the number of markers to allow cells with up to 10-fold differences in marker intensity to be counted together ;; filter=Argument in countCells to adjust light filtering for memory efficiency ;; type=Argument in outlierGate (e.g., "upper") to specify which side of the distribution to gate out ;; p=Percentile in intensityRanges (e.g., 0.05) to cap minimum and maximum intensities at the 5th and 95th percentiles to avoid outlier skewing ;; run=Logical in interpretSpheres indicating whether to run the Shiny app automatically
- alternatives: Rtsne=Suggested instead of PCA (prcomp) for dimensionality reduction of complex datasets ;; selectorPlot=Interactive framework from the scran package to select and save hyperspheres ;; pickBestMarkers=Function from scran to identify the best markers distinguishing cells in one subpopulation ;; normalizeBatch=Used for range-based or warping-based normalization across multiple batches of separately barcoded samples ;; expandRadius=Used to smooth over batch effects when no barcoding is available
- when_to_use: When analyzing mass cytometry (CyTOF) data to identify cell subpopulations that change in abundance between conditions (e.g., drug treatment vs control, before/after stimulation).
- pitfalls: calcNormFactors=Do not use calcNormFactors from edgeR in this context, as its assumptions may not apply to mass cytometry data; instead, normalize by total cell count per sample by setting lib.size=cd$totals ;; simple BH correction=Applying simple BH correction to hypersphere p-values fails to account for different densities of hyperspheres in different parts of the high-dimensional space; use spatialFDR instead ;; sample-specific gating=Avoid sample-specific transformation/gating functions to prevent spurious differences; pool cells first using poolCells ;; gating markers=Markers used for gating (e.g., DNA markers, QC markers, dead/alive markers) should be discarded before downstream counting and testing

workflows.name: differential_abundance_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify differentially abundant cell subpopulations between conditions in mass cytometry data by counting cells in hyperspheres and controlling the spatial FDR.
input: FCS files (mass cytometry raw intensity data)
workflows.stages: 1. Pool cells across samples using poolCells ;; 2. Estimate transformation parameters using estimateLogicle and apply them ;; 3. Gate out uninteresting cells using outlierGate and subset the data ;; 4. Prepare cell data for counting using prepareCellData ;; 5. Count cells into hyperspheres using countCells ;; 6. Filter low-abundance hyperspheres and perform differential abundance testing using edgeR (QL framework) ;; 7. Control the spatial FDR using spatialFDR ;; 8. Visualize results using plotSphereLogFC, intensityRanges, and plotSphereIntensity ;; 9. Identify non-redundant hyperspheres using findFirstSphere and interpret them interactively using interpretSpheres
workflows.code:
ncells <- 20000
nda <- 200
nmarkers <- 31
down.pos <- 1.8
up.pos <- 1.2
conditions <- rep(c("A", "B"), each=3)
combined <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(ncells*nmarkers, 1.5, 0.6), ncol=nmarkers),
                  matrix(rnorm(nda*nmarkers, down.pos, 0.3), ncol=nmarkers),
                  matrix(rnorm(nda*nmarkers, up.pos, 0.3), ncol=nmarkers))
combined[,31] <- rnorm(nrow(combined), 1, 0.5) # last marker is a QC marker. 
combined <- 10^combined # raw intensity values                  
sample.id <- c(sample(length(conditions), ncells, replace=TRUE), 
               sample(which(conditions=="A"), nda, replace=TRUE), 
               sample(which(conditions=="B"), nda, replace=TRUE))
colnames(combined) <- paste0("Marker", seq_len(nmarkers))

library(ncdfFlow)
collected.exprs <- list()
for (i in seq_along(conditions)) {
    stuff <- list(combined[sample.id==i,,drop=FALSE])
    names(stuff) <- paste0("Sample", i)
    collected.exprs[[i]] <- poolCells(stuff)
}
names(collected.exprs) <- paste0("Sample", seq_along(conditions))
collected.exprs <- ncdfFlowSet(as(collected.exprs, "flowSet"))

pool.ff <- poolCells(collected.exprs)

library(flowCore)
trans <- estimateLogicle(pool.ff, colnames(pool.ff))
proc.ff <- transform(pool.ff, trans)

gate.31 <- outlierGate(proc.ff, "Marker31", type="upper")
gate.31
filter.31 <- filter(proc.ff, gate.31)
summary(filter.31@subSet)

processed.exprs <- transform(collected.exprs, trans)

processed.exprs <- Subset(processed.exprs, gate.31)

processed.exprs <- processed.exprs[,1:30]

cd <- prepareCellData(processed.exprs)

cd <- countCells(cd, tol=0.5)

head(assay(cd))

head(intensities(cd))

library(edgeR)
y <- DGEList(assay(cd), lib.size=cd$totals)

keep <- aveLogCPM(y) >= aveLogCPM(5, mean(cd$totals))
cd <- cd[keep,]
y <- y[keep,]

design <- model.matrix(~factor(conditions))
y <- estimateDisp(y, design)
fit <- glmQLFit(y, design, robust=TRUE)
res <- glmQLFTest(fit, coef=2)

qvals <- spatialFDR(intensities(cd), res$table$PValue)

is.sig <- qvals <= 0.05
summary(is.sig)

sig.coords <- intensities(cd)[is.sig,]
sig.res <- res$table[is.sig,]
coords <- prcomp(sig.coords)

plotSphereLogFC(coords$x[,1], coords$x[,2], sig.res$logFC)

par(mfrow=c(6,5), mar=c(2.1, 1.1, 3.1, 1.1))
limits <- intensityRanges(cd, p=0.05)
all.markers <- markernames(cd)
for (i in order(all.markers)) { 
    plotSphereIntensity(coords$x[,1], coords$x[,2], sig.coords[,i],
        irange=limits[,i], main=all.markers[i])
}

nonred <- findFirstSphere(intensities(cd), res$table$PValue)
summary(nonred)

all.coords <- prcomp(intensities(cd))
app <- interpretSpheres(cd, select=nonred, metrics=res$table, run=FALSE,
                        red.coords=all.coords$x[,1:2], red.highlight=is.sig)
